name: Chess
summary: Chess against WOPR. You play White and move first, and WOPR answers with its move as squares, such as WOPR: D7D5.
howToPlay: Checkmate WOPR's king. Stalemate and too few pieces to mate are draws.
At YOUR MOVE: type a move as squares (E2E4, E2-E4 or E2 E4) or in algebraic notation (NF3, EXD5, O-O).
To promote a pawn, type E7E8Q or E8=Q. E7E8 alone makes a queen.
A move that is not legal gets ILLEGAL MOVE. Type RESIGN to give up.

controls.does: move by squares, from then to (E2-E4 and E2 E4 work too)
move in algebraic notation; EXD5 is a pawn capture
castle on the king's side or the queen's side
leave the game and go back to WOPR

tips: WOPR takes loose pieces. Before each move, check that every piece you have is defended.
WOPR looks only a few moves ahead, so a slow plan can get past it.
Start with a seed (wopr chess -s 1) and WOPR plays the same way every time, which helps you practise.

screenshots.caption: After E2E4 D7D5 and EXD5, WOPR's queen takes back on D5.
NC3 attacks the queen, and WOPR answers D5E6 with check.
Both sides have castled or brought out their knights.
